title: Orphan Edge Cleanup
definition: A phase in the infrastructure status which involves identifying and resolving unconnected edges, or orphan edges, in the data structure.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a game of Pac-Man. Orphan edges are like those lonely dots that Pac-Man can't eat because they're not connected to the main path. They need a cleanup to be part of the whole game.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: In a graph structure, orphan edges are edges that are not connected to any nodes. This phase of the infrastructure status involves identifying these orphan edges and deciding how to handle them.
difficulty_levels.expert: The concept of orphan edge cleanup builds upon graph theory and data structure principles. It is a critical step in data quality assurance to ensure the integrity of the data structure. However, it presents challenges such as deciding whether to create a new phase or fold it into an existing one, and considering the philosophical implications of unconnected data.

extra_fields.insight: The decision to create a new phase or fold it into an existing one highlights the continuous evolution and adaptation of the infrastructure status.
